## 1 Preparations

### 1.1 Log on to the API Tool console

You can log on to the API Tool console from the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Prerequisites Before you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, the endpoint of the console is obtained from the deployment personnel. A browser is available. We recommend that you use Google Chrome. Procedure
1. Enter the URL of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console in the address bar and press Enter.
2. Enter your username and password.
Obtain the username and password that are used to log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console from the operations administrator. Not e When you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console for the first time, you must change the password of your account. For security purposes, your password must meet the minimum complexity requirements. The password must be 10 to 32 characters in length and must contain at least two of the following character types: Uppercase or lowercase letters Digits Special characters, which include ! @ # $ %
3. Click Log On.
4. If your account has multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled, perform corresponding operations
in the following scenarios: You log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console for the first time after MFA is enabled by the administrator. a. On the Bind Virtual MFA Device page, bind an MFA device. b. Enter the username and password again as in Step 2 and click Log On. c. Enter a six-digit MFA verification code and click Aut hent icat e. You have enabled MFA and bound an MFA device. Enter a six-digit MFA verification code and click Aut hent icat e. Not e For more information, see the Bind a virtual MFA device to enable MFA topic in A psara Uni-manager Management Console User Guide.
5. In the top navigation bar, choose Product s > Ot hers > API T ool.

### 1.2 View the information about an operation

operation When you use a service SDK to call an operation of the service, you must obtain the service name, operation name, and API version. This topic describes how to view the information about an operation. Context The operations on the API Directory page are for reference only. For information about how to call operations, see API references of the corresponding services. If the information on the API Directory page is inconsistent with that in the API reference of the corresponding service, the information in the API reference takes precedence. Procedure
1. Log on to the API Tool console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click API Direct ory.
3. On the API Direct ory page, select the required service from the drop-down list, enter a keyword
of an operation name in the search box, and then click Search.
4. View and record the service name, operation name, and API version.

### 1.3 Obtain an AccessKey pair

AccessKey pairs are classified into AccessKey pairs assigned by Resource Access Management (RAM) and AccessKey pairs assigned by Security Token Service (STS). You can use either type of AccessKey pair for authentication when you call operations. This topic describes how to obtain an AccessKey pair that is assigned by RAM. Context An AccessKey pair is used to verify the identity of request senders. An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret that are used to implement symmetric encryption. The AccessKey ID is used to identify a user. The AccessKey secret is used to encrypt the signature string. You can use RAM or STS to assign an AccessKey pair for authentication. Use RAM to assign an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret to a third party. Use STS to assign an AccessKey ID, an AccessKey secret, and a security token to a third party. For more information, see Obtain an STS AccessKey pair. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides AccessKey pairs for personal accounts or organizations. Only the administrators of level-1 organizations and operations administrators can obtain the AccessKey pairs of organizations. We recommend that you use the AccessKey pairs of personal accounts to call the operations provided by the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and cloud services. If you use the AccessKey pair of a personal account, you must add the following parameters in request headers for access control. If you do not add the parameters, an error may occur. The error indicates that permissions are insufficient.

> **Warning:** The AccessKey pair of a personal account is managed by the permission system of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. The AccessKey pair of an organization has more permissions than the AccessKey pair of a personal account. If you want to obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization, make sure that you are authorized by an administrator. This helps ensure security.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| x-acs-regionid | The ID of the region. Example: cn-hangzhou-*. |
| x-acs-organizationid | The ID of the organization in the Apsara Uni- manager Management Console. For more information about how to obtain organization IDs, see the GetOrganizationList section in Apsara Uni- manager Management Console Developer Guide. |
| x-acs-resourcegroupid | The ID of the resource set in the Apsara Uni- manager Management Console. For more information about how to obtain resource set IDs, see the ListResourceGroup section in Apsara Uni- manager Management Console Developer Guide. |
| x-acs-instanceid | The ID of the instance on which you want to perform operations. For example, you can obtain the ID of an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance from the ECS instance list. |

Obtain the AccessKey pair of a personal account To obtain the AccessKey pair of a personal account, perform the following operations:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the upper-right corner of the homepage, move the pointer over the profile picture and click User
Inf ormat ion.
3. In the AccessKey Pair section, view the AccessKey pair of your account.
Not e An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. These credentials provide full permissions on cloud resources within your account. You must keep the AccessKey pair confidential. Obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization To obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization, perform the following operations:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an administrator.
2. In the top navigation bar, click Ent erprise.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose Resources > Organizat ions.
4. In the organization list, click the name of the level-1 organization whose AccessKey pair you want
to obtain.
5. Click Management Accesskey.
6. In the dialog box that appears, view the AccessKey pair of the organization.

### 1.4 Obtain an AccessKey pair assigned by STS

assigned by STS This topic describes how to use Security Token Service (STS) to make API calls. Background information Alibaba Cloud STS allows you to manage temporary credentials to your Alibaba Cloud resources. You can use STS to make API calls. An AccessKey pair assigned by STS consists of an AccessKey ID, an AccessKey secret, and a security token. When you use STS to make API calls, you must use an AccessKey pair assigned by STS. For more information about STS, see What is STS? Procedure
1. Obtain your `RAM role` .
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. Click the profile picture in the upper-right corner of the page and click User Inf ormat ion. iii. Click View Current Role Policy. In the View Policies of Current Role dialog box, view your `RAM role` .
2. Obtain the AccessKey pair assigned by STS.
Not e You must use the actual values to replace the variables in the following sample code. The angle brackets <> are not retained in the final code. The following list describes the variables: <yourRegionID>: Replace it with the actual region ID. <yourAccessKeyID>: Replace it with your AccessKey ID. <yourAccessKeySecret>: Replace it with your AccessKey secret. <yourRoleSessionName>: Replace it with your current session name. <yourRoleArn>: Replace it with the Alibaba Cloud Resource Name (ARN) of your RAM role. "sts.aliyuns.com": Replace it with the endpoint of STS.

```
public static void main(String[] args) {
    // Create a DefaultAcsClient instance and initialize it.
    Replace <yourRegionID>, <yourAccessKeyID>, and <yourAccessKeySecret> with the actua
l region ID, your AccessKey ID, and your AccessKey secret.
    DefaultProfile profile = DefaultProfile.getProfile("<yourRegionID>", "<yourAccessKe
yID>", "<yourAccessKeySecret>");
    HttpClientConfig clientConfig = HttpClientConfig.getDefault();
    clientConfig.setIgnoreSSLCerts(true);
    clientConfig.setProtocolType(ProtocolType.HTTPS);
    profile.setHttpClientConfig(clientConfig);
    IAcsClient client = new DefaultAcsClient(profile);
    String assumeRole = callAssumeRole(client);
    if (StringUtils.isEmpty(assumeRole)) return;
    JSONObject assumeRoleJson = JSONObject.parseObject(assumeRole);
    JSONObject credentials = assumeRoleJson.getJSONObject("Credentials");
    // Obtain the AccessKey pair assigned by STS.
    String stsAK = credentials.getString("AccessKeyId");
    String stsSK = credentials.getString("AccessKeySecret");
    String stsToken = credentials.getString("SecurityToken");
```

`}`

```java
private static String callAssumeRole(IAcsClient client) {
    CommonRequest request = new CommonRequest();
    // Replace "sts.aliyuns.com" with the endpoint of STS. The format of an STS endpoin
t is sts-vpc.${global:region}.${global:internet-domain}.
    request.setSysDomain("sts.aliyuns.com");
    request.setSysProduct("Sts");
    request.setSysAction("AssumeRole");
    request.setSysVersion("2015-04-01");
    request.setSysMethod(MethodType.POST);
    request.setHttpContentType(FormatType.FORM);
    // The business parameter. Specify an alias for the current session. Replace "<your
RoleSessionName>" with the actual session name.
    request.putQueryParameter("RoleSessionName", "<yourRoleSessionName>");
    // The ARN of your RAM role. Replace "<yourRoleArn>" with the ARN of your RAM role
that is obtained in the previous step.
    request.putQueryParameter("RoleArn", "<yourRoleArn>");
    try {
        CommonResponse response = client.getCommonResponse(request);
        return response.getData();
    } catch (ServerException e) {
        System.out.println(e.getErrCode());
        System.out.println(e.getErrMsg());
    } catch (ClientException e) {
        System.out.println(e.getErrCode());
        System.out.println(e.getErrMsg());
```

### 1.5 Obtain an endpoint

This topic describes how to obtain the endpoint of an Apsara Stack Security service. Context To use the POP gateway to call the API operations of a cloud service, you must specify the endpoint of the cloud service. You can obtain the endpoint from Apsara Stack onsite O&M engineers. You can also perform the following steps to obtain the endpoint. Procedure
1. Log on to the Apsara Infrastructure Management console. In the left-side navigation pane, choose
Operat ions > Clust er Operat ions.
2. On the Clust ers page, enter yundun-advance in the Project search box and enter BasicThinCluster
in the Clust er search box. Click the name of the BasicT hinClust er cluster or click Operat ions in the Actions column of the BasicT hinClust er cluster.
3. On the Clust er Det ails page, click the Clust er Conf igurat ion tab, find and open the kv.conf file,
and then obtain the values of the region and internet-domain parameters.
4. Obtain the value of the EndpointPre parameter. For more information, see Common parameters.
5. Obtain the endpoint based on the region, internet-domain, and EndpointPre parameters.
The endpoint of a cloud service is in the following format:

```
${EndpointPre}.${global:region}.${global:internet-domain}
```

What to do next If you want to call the API operations of Apsara Stack Security services from the service domain or O&M domain, you must configure the hosts file on your computer.
1. Obtain the virtual IP address (VIP) of the POP.
i. Click Back t o Old Version to switch to Apsara Infrastructure Management of the previous version. In the top navigation bar, choose Operat ions > Clust er Operat ions. ii. In the cluster list, enter webappAll in the Project search box and enter StandardCloudCluster in the Clust er search box. Click the name of the first St andardCloudClust er cluster. iii. In the Clust er Resource section, click the icon to the right of the Type parameter, select Cont ains from the drop-down list, and then enter `vip` as the filter condition to locate the O&M domain, management domain, and service domain. Not e The following list describes the cluster resources that correspond to the three domains: O&M domain: The Name parameter of the cluster resource is pop-vip-ops. Management domain: The Name parameter of the cluster resource is pop-vipmgmt . Service domain: The Name parameter of the cluster resource is pop-vip-biz. iv. Right-click the value in the Result volume for the O&M domain, management domain, or service domain and select Show More. In the Details dialog box, obtain the value of the vip_ip parameter.
2. Configure the hosts file on your local computer.

```xml
<vip_ip> <Endpoint of the API that you want to request>
```

## 2 Call examples

### 2.1 Call examples for SDK for Java

#### 2.1.1 Quick start

This topic describes how to obtain and use Apsara Stack SDK for Java. Prerequisites An Apsara Stack tenant account that has the required permissions and an AccessKey pair that consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret are obtained before you can use Apsara Stack SDK for Java. You can view and obtain your AccessKey pair in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For more information, see Obtain an AccessKey pair. For more information about how to obtain the endpoint, see Obtain an endpoint. Java Development Kit (JDK) 1.8 or later is installed before you can use Apsara Stack SDK for Java. Installation If you use Apache Maven to manage a Java project, you need to only import the JAR file of Apsara Stack SDK for Java to the pom.xml file of the project. If you want to use Apsara Stack Security SDK for Java, you must install the core library of Apsara Stack SDK for Java. We recommend that you use V4.5.17 or later of the core library. Usage To use Apsara Stack SDK for Java, perform the following steps:
1. Create a DefaultAcsClient instance and initialize the instance.
2. Create an API request and configure the required parameters.
3. Initiate the API request and process the response or exception.
Not e In the following code, replace the variables with actual values. Delete the angle brackets <> in the final code. The following section describes the variables: <your-region-id>: Replace this variable with the region ID. <your-access-key-id>: Replace this variable with your AccessKey ID. <your-access-key-secret>: Replace this variable with your AccessKey secret. <your-endpoint>: Replace this variable with the endpoint of the service. <API-version>: Replace this variable with the version of the API. <your-action>: Replace this variable with the name of the API operation.

```java
import com.aliyuncs.CommonRequest; import com.aliyuncs.CommonResponse; import com.aliyuncs.DefaultAcsClient; import com.aliyuncs.IAcsClient; import com.aliyuncs.exceptions.ClientException; import com.aliyuncs.exceptions.ServerException; import com.aliyuncs.profile.DefaultProfile; public class Sample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Create a DefaultAcsClient instance and initialize the instance.
        DefaultProfile profile = DefaultProfile.getProfile(
            "<your-region-id>",          // The ID of the region.
            "<your-access-key-id>",      // The AccessKey ID.
            "<your-access-key-secret>"); // The AccessKey secret.
        IAcsClient client = new DefaultAcsClient(profile);
        // Create an API request and configure the required parameters.
        CommonRequest request = new CommonRequest();
        request.setDomain("<your-endpooint>");// The endpoint of the service.
        request.setVersion("<API-version>");// The version of the API.
        request.setAction("<your-action>");// The name of the API operation.
        request.putQueryParameter("PageNumber", "1");
        request.putQueryParameter("PageSize", "30");
        try {
            CommonResponse response = client.getCommonResponse(request);
            System.out.println(response.getData());
        } catch (ServerException e) {
            // TODO Auto-generated catch block
            e.printStackTrace();
        } catch (ClientException e) {
            // TODO Auto-generated catch block
            e.printStackTrace();
```

`}` `}` `}`

#### 2.1.2 Use SDK

##### 2.1.2.1 Install SDK for Java

This topic describes how to install and use Apsara Stack Security SDK for Java. Apsara Stack SDK for Java supports Java Development Kit (JDK) 1.8 or later. You can install Apsara Stack SDK for Java by adding Maven dependencies or downloading the SDK. For more information, visit Alibaba Cloud SDKs. If you want to use Apsara Stack Security SDK for Java, you must install the core library of Apsara Stack SDK for Java. We recommend that you use V4.5.17 or later of the core library. When you install the core library, you must add the following dependency to the pom.xml file. For more information about the specific SDK version, visit Alibaba Cloud SDKs.

```xml
<!-- Alibaba Cloud SDK for Java --> <dependency>
    <groupId>com.aliyun</groupId>
    <artifactId>aliyun-java-sdk-core</artifactId>
    <version>4.5.17</version>
</dependency>
```

##### 2.1.2.2 Use CommonRequest to call API operations

Not e If you want to call the API operations of a service that does not provide SDKs, you can use CommonRequest. You can use CommonRequest to call API operations. Benefits CommonRequest provides the following benefits:
1. Lightweight: You need to only download the core package. You do not need to download and
install SDKs of services.
2. Easy to use: You can call the newly released API operations of a service without the need to
update the SDK for the service.
3. Fast iteration.
Use CommonRequest to call an API operation Apsara Stack services provide RPC and RESTful APIs. The request method of CommonRequest varies based on the style of the API that you want to call. In most cases, an API uses the RPC style if the API operations include the Action parameter. An API uses the RESTful style if the API operations include the PathPattern parameter. All API operations of a service use the same API style. The API of each service supports only one style. If you pass an invalid identifier, another API operation may be called, or the `ApiNotFound` error is returned. If you want to send a CommonRequest request, you must obtain the values of the following parameters. For more information about the values of these parameters, see the API reference in DocumentationDocumentation. You can also visit OpenAPI Explorer to obtain the parameter values of API operations for some services. Endpoint: the endpoint of a service. Version: the version of the API. The version is in the YYYY-MM-DD format. Operation information: the name of the API operation that you want to call. The APIs of most Apsara Stack services, such as Threat Detection Service, are RPC APIs. If you want to call an RPC API operation, you must obtain the value of the Action parameter, and then specify the value in the `request.ApiName = "<Action>"` format. If you want to call a RESTful API operation of a service, such as Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK), you must obtain the value of the PathPattern parameter, and then specify the RESTful path in the `request.PathPattern = "<PathPattern>"` format. Example: Call an RPC API operation The following sample code shows how to use CommonRequest to call an API operation of Apsara Stack Security:

```java
import com.aliyuncs.CommonRequest; import com.aliyuncs.CommonResponse; import com.aliyuncs.DefaultAcsClient; import com.aliyuncs.IAcsClient; import com.aliyuncs.exceptions.ClientException; import com.aliyuncs.exceptions.ServerException; import com.aliyuncs.profile.DefaultProfile; public class Sample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Create a DefaultAcsClient instance and initialize the instance.
        DefaultProfile profile = DefaultProfile.getProfile(
            "<your-region-id>",          // The ID of the region.
            "<your-access-key-id>",      // The AccessKey ID.
            "<your-access-key-secret>"); // The AccessKey secret.
        IAcsClient client = new DefaultAcsClient(profile);
        // Create an API request and specify parameters.
        CommonRequest request = new CommonRequest();
        request.setDomain("<your-endpoint>");// The endpoint of the service.
        request.setVersion("<API-version>");// The version of the API.
        request.setAction("<your-action>");// The name of the API operation.
        request.putQueryParameter("PageNumber", "1");
        request.putQueryParameter("PageSize", "30");
        try {
            CommonResponse response = client.getCommonResponse(request);
            System.out.println(response.getData());
        } catch (ServerException e) {
            // TODO Auto-generated catch block
            e.printStackTrace();
        } catch (ClientException e) {
            // TODO Auto-generated catch block
            e.printStackTrace();
```

`}` `}` `}`

### 2.2 Call examples for SDK for Python

#### 2.2.1 Quick start

This topic describes how to obtain and use the SDK for Python. Prerequisites An authorized account and an AccessKey pair (AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret) are obtained. For more information, see Obtain an AccessKey pair. The endpoint of a service is obtained. For more information, see . Install the core library of the SDK for Python If you use Python 2.x, run the following command:

```
pip install aliyun-python-sdk-core
```

If you use Python 3.x, run the following command:

```
pip3 install aliyun-python-sdk-core-v3
```

Use the SDK for Python To use the SDK for Python, perform the following steps:
1. Create a client instance.
When you create a client instance, you must obtain a region ID, AccessKey ID, and AccessKey secret.
2. Create an API request and specify the required parameters.
3. Initiate the API request and process the response or exception.
Not e In the following code, replace the variables with actual values. Delete the angle brackets <> in the final code. The following section describes the variables: <your_region_id>: Replace the value of this parameter with the region ID. <your_access_key_id>: Replace the the value of this parameter with your AccessKey ID. <your_access_key_secret>: Replace the value of this parameter with your AccessKey secret. <your-endpoint>: Replace the value of this parameter with the endpoint of the service. <API-version>: Replace the value of this parameter with the version of the API. <your-action>: Replace the value of this parameter with the name of the API operation.

```bash
from aliyunsdkcore.client import AcsClient from aliyunsdkcore.request import CommonRequest client = AcsClient('{your_access_key_id}', '{your_access_key_secret}', '{your_region_id}') request = CommonRequest() request.set_domain('<your-endpoint>')// The endpoint of the service. request.set_version('<API-version>')// The version of the API. request.set_action_name('<your-action>')// The name of the API operation.
# or:
# request =
CommonRequest(domain='<your-endpoint>', version='<API-version>', action_name='<your-action>') request.add_query_param('PageNumber', '1') request.add_query_param('PageSize', '30') response = client.do_action_with_exception(request)
```

## 3 Common parameters

Common request parameters Common request parameters must be included in all Apsara Stack Security API requests. Table of common request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Requir ed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Format | String | No | The format in which to return the response. Set the value to JSON. |
| Version | String | Yes | The version number of the API. Specify the version number in the YYYY-MM-DD format. Valid values: If you call the API operations of the cloud service whose service code is Auditprivate, set the value to 2018-01-16. If you call the API operations of the cloud service whose service code is yundunnextsoc, set the value to 2019-07-23. If you call the API operations of the cloud service whose service code is Sas, set the value to 2018-12-03. If you call the API operations of the cloud service whose service code is aegis, set the value to 2016-11-11. If you call the API operations of the cloud service whose service code is yundun-css, set the value to 2021-10-11. If you call the API operations of the cloud service whose service code is secspy, set the value to 2019-08-05. If you call the API operations of the cloud service whose service code is Ddosprivate, set the value to 2018-01-16. If you call the API operations of the cloud service whose service code is hsm-private, set the value to 2018-06-30. If you call the API operations of the cloud service whose service code is Cloudfw, set the value to 2017-12-07. If you call the API operations of the cloud service whose service code is Sddp, set the value to 2019-01-03. If you call the API operations of the cloud service whose service code is semawaf, set the value to 2020-07-01. If you call the API operations of the cloud service whose service code is soar, set the value to 2018-12-03. |
| AccessKeyId | String | Yes | The AccessKey ID provided to you by Apsara Stack. |
| AccessKeySecre t | String | Yes | The AccessKey secret provided to you by Apsara Stack. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | The region ID of the service. |

ers

| Parameter | Type | Requir ed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Product | String | Yes | The name of the service to which the API operation belongs. Valid values: Audit privat e: basic components of Apsara Stack Security yundunnext soc: Security Operations Center (SOC) Sas: Threat Detection Service aegis: Server Guard yundun-css: Container Production secspy: Network Detection and Response Ddosprivat e: Anti-DDoS Service hsm-privat e: Data Encryption Service Cloudf w: Cloud Firewall Sddp: Sensitive Data Discovery and Protection (SDDP) semawaf : Web Application Firewall (WAF) soar: Security Orchestration and Automation Response (SOAR) |
| EndpointPre | String | Yes | The prefix in the endpoint of the service to which the API operation belongs. Valid values: audit privat e: the prefix in the endpoint of basic components of Apsara Stack Security yundunnext soc-pop: the prefix in the endpoint of SOC t ds: the prefix in the endpoint of Threat Detection Service aegis: the prefix in the endpoint of Server Guard yundun-css: the prefix in the endpoint of Container Protection secspy-share: the prefix in the endpoint of Network Detection and Response ddosprivat e: the prefix in the endpoint of Anti-DDoS Service hsmprivat e: the prefix in the endpoint of Data Encryption Service cloudf w: the prefix in the endpoint of Cloud Firewall sddp-api: the prefix in the endpoint of SDDP semawaf : the prefix in the endpoint of WAF soar: the prefix in the endpoint of SOAR |

Common response parameters API responses use the HTTP response format: A 2xx status code indicates a successful call. A 4xx or 5xx status code indicates a failed call. Responses are returned in the JSON format. Every response returns a unique RequestID regardless of whether the call is successful.

## 4 Server Guard

### 4.1 Asset management

#### 4.1.1 DescribeGroupSummary

You can call this operation to obtain a list of asset groups. Request parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeGroupSummary. |

Response parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | The GUID generated by Alibaba Cloud for the request. |
| Count | Integer | The number of asset groups. |
| Groups | List | The information about asset groups. For more information, see the following parameter descriptions. |
| GroupId | Long | The asset group ID. |
| GroupIndex | Integer | The sequence number of the asset group. |
| GroupLevel | Integer | The level of the asset group. |
| GroupName | String | The name of the asset group. |
| GroupFather | Integer | The ID of the parent asset group. |
| GroupFlag | Integer | The type of the asset group. Valid values: 1: indicates a non-leaf node group that contains child asset groups. 0: indicates a leaf node group. |
| MachineNum | Integer | The number of ECS instances contained in the group. |

Error codes For more information about the error codes that this operation can return, see Error codes. Examples Sample requests

```
https://aegis.[ RegionId].example.com/?Action=DescribeGroupSummary &<Common request parameters>
```

Sample responses (JSON format)

```json
   "GroupFlag":1,
   "GroupName":"Test group 21",
   "GroupIndex":1,
   "MachineNum":0,
   "GroupId":346
```

#### 4.2.8 DescribeGroupedVul

You can call this operation to query information about the specified vulnerability group. The vulnerability management feature can display detected vulnerability records by group. A vulnerability group contains all servers with a specific vulnerability detected by Server Guard. Request parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeGroupedVul. |
| PageSize | Integer | No | The maximum number of records to be displayed on each page of the query output. Default value: 20. |
| CurrentPage | Integer | No | The current page number. Default value: 1. |
| Dealed | String | No | Indicates whether the vulnerability has been handled. Valid values: Y: indicates that the vulnerability has been handled. N: indicates that the vulnerability has not been handled. |
| Direction | String | No | The sorting mode of vulnerabilities in the vulnerability group. Valid values: asc: indicates sorting in ascending order. desc: indicates sorting in descending order. |
| LastTsEnd | Long | No | The end time of the last detection of the vulnerability. |
| LastTsStart | Long | No | The start time of the last detection of the vulnerability. |

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Level | String | No | The severity of the vulnerability. Valid values: serious: critical high: important medium: moderate low: low |
| Name | String | No | The name of the vulnerability. |
| Necessity | String | No | The necessity for fixing the vulnerability. Valid values: asap: indicates that the vulnerability must be fixed as soon as possible. later: indicates that the vulnerability can be fixed later. nntf: indicates that the vulnerability can be ignored. |
| OrderBy | String | No | The field based on which the vulnerabilities in the vulnerability group are sorted. You can specify other request parameters for sorting order. |
| PatchId | Long | No | The ID of the patch used to fix the vulnerability. |
| Product | String | No | The product where the vulnerability exists. |

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| StatusList | String | No | The status of the vulnerability. Valid values: 1: indicates that the vulnerability has not been fixed. 2: indicates that the vulnerability fix failed. 3: indicates that the server has failed to be rolled back to the version before the vulnerability fix. 4: indicates that the vulnerability is being fixed. 5: indicates that the server is being rolled back to the version before the vulnerability fix. 6: indicates that the vulnerability fix is being verified. 7: indicates that the vulnerability has been fixed successfully. 8: indicates that the vulnerability has been fixed successfully, and that the server is waiting for restart. 9: indicates that the server has been rolled back to the version before the vulnerability fix. 10: indicates that the vulnerability has been ignored. 11: indicates that the server has been rolled back to the version before the vulnerability fix, and that the server is waiting for restart. 12: indicates that the vulnerability does not exist. 20: indicates that the vulnerability is invalid. Not e The statuses are specified in a single parameter, separated with commas (,). |
| Type | String | No | The type of the vulnerability. |
| Uuids | String | No | The UUID of the server. Separate multiple UUIDs with commas (,). |

Response parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | The GUID generated by Alibaba Cloud for the request. |
| CurrentPage | Integer | The current page number. |
| PageSize | Integer | The maximum number of records displayed on a page. |
| TotalCount | Integer | The total number of returned records. |
| GroupedVulItems | Array | The information about the vulnerability group. For more information, see the following parameter descriptions. |
| AliasName | String | The alias of the vulnerability. |
| AsapCount | Integer | The number of assets to be fixed as soon as possible. |
| Count | Integer | The total number of vulnerabilities. |
| GmtLast | Long | The last time when the vulnerability was detected. |
| HandledCount | Integer | The total number of vulnerabilities handled. |
| Level | String | The severity of the vulnerability. |
| Name | String | The name of the vulnerability. |
| PendingCount | Integer | The number of vulnerabilities that have not been handled. |
| Product | String | The product affected by the vulnerability. |
| Status | Integer | The status of the vulnerability. |
| TotalCount | Integer | The total number of vulnerabilities. |
| Type | String | The type of the vulnerability. |

Error codes For more information about the error codes that this operation can return, see Error codes. Examples Sample requests

### 7.3 Security alerts

#### 7.3.1 DescribeAlarmEventList

Queries alert events on the Alerts page. An alert event consists of alerts and exceptions. Each alert event is related to multiple exceptions. Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeAlarmEve ntList | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeAlarmEventList. |
| CurrentPage | Integer | Yes | 1 | The page number of the current page. Pages start from page 1. Default value: 1. |
| From | String | Yes | sas | The ID of the request source. Set the value to sas. |
| PageSize | String | Yes | 20 | The number of entries to return on each page. Default value: 20. |
| SourceIp | String | No | 1.2.3.4 | The source IP address of the request. |
| Lang | String | No | zh | The natural language of the request and response. Valid values: zh: Chinese en: English |

Service (TDS)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dealed | String | No | Y | The status of the alert event. Valid values: N: unhandled Y: handled |
| Levels | String | No | serious | The severity levels of the alert events. Separate multiple levels with commas (,). Valid values: serious suspicious remind |
| Remark | String | No | database server _ | The name of the alert, or the asset information. |
| GroupId | String | No | tst*** | The group ID of the affected asset. |
| AlarmEventName | String | No | DDoS trojans | The name of the alert event. |
| AlarmEventType | String | No | Malicious process (cloud threat detection) | The type of the alert event. |

Service (TDS)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OperateErrorCode List.N | RepeatLi st | No | ignore. Success | Alert handling result code N. The value is in the format of Operation type.Operation result code. Operation types include: Common: performs common operations. deal: handles the alert. ignore: ignores the alert. offline handled: marks the alert as _ handled. mark mis info: marks the alerts as _ _ false positives by adding them to the whitelist. rm mark mis info: cancels false _ _ _ positives by removing the alerts from the whitelist. quara: quarantines the source file of the malicious process. kill and quara: kills the malicious _ _ process and quarantines the source file. kill virus: deletes the source file of _ the malicious process. block ip: blocks the source IP _ addresses. manual handled: manually handles _ the alert. Operation result codes: Success: The operation is successful. Failure: The operation fails. AgentOffline: The agent is offline. |

### 7.4 Configuration assessment

#### 7.4.1 DescribeRiskItemType

Queries types of check items for cloud service configurations. Each check item is categorized into a type. Types of check items include identity authentication and permissions, network access control, log auditing, data security, monitoring and alerting, and basic security protection. Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeRiskItem Type | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeRiskItemType. |
| Lang | String | No | zh | The natural language of the request and response. Valid values: zh: Chinese en: English |
| SourceIp | String | No | 1.2.3.4 | The source IP address of the request. |

Response parameters

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| List | Array |   | The information about the check item. |
| Id | Long | 1 | The ID of the check item. |
| Title | String | Identity authentication and permissions | The type of the check item. Example: Identity authentication and permissions. |
| RequestId | String | 3B3F3A90-46A5- 4023-A2D8- D68B14262F96 | The ID of the request. |

#### 7.6.2 DescribeStratety

Queries the configurations of baseline check policies. Request parameters Service (TDS)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeStratety | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeStratety. |
| Lang | String | No | zh | The natural language of the request and response. Valid values: zh: Chinese en: English |
| SourceIp | String | No | 1.2.3.4 | The source IP address of the request. |
| StrategyIds | String | No | test1,test2,test3 | The IDs of the baseline check policies. Separate multiple IDs with commas (,). |

Response parameters

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | 16B9826C-B99F- 4F8A-8048- EA81D6D3DE8B | The ID of the request. |
| Strategies | Array |   | The information about the baseline check policy. |
| ConfigTargets | Array |   | The information about the group associated with the baseline check policy. |
| Flag | String | add | The related ID. |
| Target | String | 3259405 | The ID of the related group. |
| TargetType | String | groupId | The type of the related group. |
| CycleDays | Integer | 1 | The cycle of the baseline check. 1: every second day 3: every fourth day 7: every eighth day 30: every 31st day |

Service (TDS)

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| CycleStartTime | Integer | 6 | The time when the baseline check starts. Valid values: 0, 6, 12, and 18. |
| EcsCount | Integer | 5 | The number of servers on which baseline checks were performed based on the specified baseline check policy. |
| ExecStatus | Integer | 1 | The execution status of the baseline check. Valid values: 1: The baseline check is not running. 2: The baseline check is running. |
| Id | Integer | 212635 | The ID of the policy. |
| Name | String | test | The name of the policy. |
| PassRate | Integer | 80 | The pass rate of the latest baseline check. |
| ProcessRate | Integer | 80 | The progress of the baseline check. |
| RiskCount | Integer | 5 | The number of selected check items. |
| Type | Integer | 1 | The type of the baseline check policy. Valid values: 1: default policy 2: custom policy |

Examples Sample requests

```
http(s)://[Endpoint]/?Action=DescribeStratety ? Lang=zh &SourceIp=127.0.0.1 &StrategyIds=1,2,3 &<Common request parameters>
```

#### 7.6.3 DescribeStrategyExecDetail

Queries the details of the latest baseline check by using a baseline check policy. The details include the time when the check is performed, the number of risk items, and the baseline risk details. Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeStrategy ExecDetail | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeStrategyExecDetail. |
| StrategyId | Integer | Yes | 1 | The ID of the baseline check policy. Not e To query the results of a baseline check that uses only one policy, you must specify the ID of the policy. You can call the DescribeStratety operation to obtain the ID. |
| SourceIp | String | No | 1.2.3.4 | The source IP address of the request. |

Response parameters

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| EndTime | String | 2019-01-08 20:11:20 | The time when the baseline check ends. |
| FailCount | Integer | 94 | The number of risk items that failed to pass the baseline check. |
| FailedEcsList | Array |   | The list of servers on which risk items were detected. |
| IP | String | 1.2.3.4 | The IP address of the instance on which the baseline check was performed. |
| InstanceName | String | Test-20180703 | The name of the instance. |
| IntranetIp | String | 1.2.3.5 | The internal IP address. |

| psara Stack Securi | ty |   | Developer Guide·Threat Detection Service (TDS |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |

| Reason | String | Detect timeout | The cause of the baseline check failure. |
|---|---|---|---|
| InProcessCount | Integer | 0 | The number of baseline check tasks that are running. |
| Percent | String | 100% | The progress of the baseline check. |
| RequestId | String | 09322632-4668- 4AD9-BD0D- 32757DEFBBA6 | The ID of the request. |
| Source | String | Manual | The type of the baseline check. Schedule Manual |
| StartTime | String | 2019-01-08 19:41:12 | The time when the baseline check starts. |
| SuccessCount | Integer | 81 | The number of check items that passed the baseline check. |

#### 7.6.5 DescribeCheckWarningDetail

Queries the details of a specific check item. Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeCheckWa rningDetail | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeCheckWarningDetail. |
| CheckWarningId | Long | Yes | 1 | The ID of the alert triggered by the check item. Not e To query the details of a specific check item, you must specify the ID of the alert triggered by the check item. You can call the DescribeCheckWarnings operation to obtain the alert ID. |

Service (TDS)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lang | String | No | zh | The natural language of the request and response. Valid values: zh: Chinese en: English |
| SourceIp | String | No | 1.2.3.4 | The source IP address of the request. |

Response parameters

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Advice | String | Fix now | The suggestion for the management of the risk item. |
| CheckId | Long | 1 | The ID of the check item. |
| Description | String | Password expiring | The additional details about the risk item. |
| Item | String | Password expiration alert | The name of the check item. |
| Level | String | high | The severity level of the risk item. high: The item is a high-risk one and highlighted in red. medium: The item is a medium-risk one and highlighted in orange. low: The item is a low-risk one and highlighted in gray. |
| Prompt | String | Password expiration alert | The prompt for the risk item. |
| RequestId | String | 09969D2C-4FAD- 429E-BFBF- 9A60DEF8BF6F | The ID of the request. |
| Type | String | Identity authentication | The type of the check item. |

Examples Sample requests Service (TDS)


```xml
   <Advice>Run the following five commands

</DescribeCheckWarningDetail>
```

## 10 Security Operations Center

### 10.1 Operations

#### 10.1.1 DescribeAttacks

You can call this operation to query attacks on users or on the platform based on specified conditions. Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeAttacks. |
| DataScope | Integer | Yes | Specifies whether the attacks on users or on the platform are queried. Valid values: 0: platform 1: users |
| SourceFrom | Integer | No | The source of attack data. |
| UserId | Long | No | The ID of the department to query. |
| PageSize | Integer | Yes | The number of attacks to return on each page. |
| PageNo | Integer | Yes | The number of the page to return. |
| AttackType | String | No | The type of the attacks to query. |
| ProcessState | Integer | No | The processing status of the attacks to query. 0: An alert has been generated on the attack. 1: The attack has been blocked. 3: The attack traffic is being scrubbed. 4: The attack traffic has been scrubbed. |
| StartTime | Long | No | The beginning of the time range to query. This value is a UNIX timestamp representing the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since the epoch time January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC. |

s Center

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| EndTime | Long | No | The end of the time range to query. This value is a UNIX timestamp representing the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since the epoch time January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC. |
| KeyWord | String | No | The keyword of the attack name or asset name. |

Response parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| PageNo | Integer | The page number of the returned page. |
| PageSize | Integer | The number of attacks returned per page. |
| Total | Integer | The total number of records. |
| RequestId | String | The ID of the request. |
| AttackName | String | The name of the attack. |
| AttackId | Long | The ID of the attack. |
| AssetType | Integer | The type of the asset. |
| Asset | String | The ID of the asset. |
| UserName | String | The name of the department. |
| RaisedTime | Long | The time of the attack. |
| ProcessState | Integer | The processing status of the attack. |
| UserId | Long | The ID of the user or department. |
| AttackType | String | The type of the attack. |
| SourceFrom | Integer | The data source of the attack. |
| AttackerIp | String | The IP address of the attacker. |
| AssetName | String | The name of the asset. |
| AssetPublicIps | String | The public IP address of the affected asset. |
| AssetPrivateIps | String | The internal IP address of the affected asset. |

#### 11.1.29 DescribeArchiveCountStat

You can call this operation to query log and event archiving statistics. Request parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeArchiveCountStat. |
| EndTime | String | No | The end time of the time frame specified for query, in timestamp format. |
| LogTypeList | String | No | The log type code. Separate multiple log types with commas (,). |
| StartTime | String | No | The start time of the time frame specified for query, in timestamp format. |

Response parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | The GUID generated by Alibaba Cloud for the request. |
| StatList | Array | A list of archiving statistics. For more information, see the following parameter descriptions. |
| LogType | Integer | The log type code. |
| StatItemList | Array | The archiving information. For more information, see the following parameter descriptions. |
| Capacity | Float | The storage space used for archiving. |
| Count | Integer | The number of archives. |
| Time | Long | The time when the statistics were collected, in timestamp format. |

Error codes For more information about the error codes that this operation can return, see Error codes. Examples Sample requests

```
https://auditprivate.[ RegionId].example.com/?Action=DescribeArchiveCountStat &EndTime=1517630399000 &LogTypeList=1,2,3 &StartTime=1497516900000 &<Common request parameters>
```
